newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen down on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen down on Monday.

text.p: Polish shares fell on Friday after a six-session gain and analysts said that after a likely dip on Monday signalled by the stronger post-price-fixing selling the market should maintain its general flat trend.
Some analysts said a slight uptrend was possible next week as profits taken from large newcomers Bank Handlowy and copper firm KGHM could flow to other stocks.

"The market needs money to go up and that money is going to go via Handlowy and KGHM and in an indirect way to other firms," said Ryszard Wojnowski, an analyst at Polish Investment Bank (PBI) brokerage.
Other analysts said concerns over the flooding in the industrial southland and the run-up to September's parliamentary election would dampen buying and could cause falls next week.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.6 percent to 15,832.8 points and turnover fell 17.6 percent to 237 million zlotys ($71.3 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 74 to 22 with 12 stocks flat.

Analysts said Handlowy, down 1.2 percent in 22.1- million-zloty ($6.8 million) trade, and KGHM, up 2.1 percent in 74.8-million-zloty ($22.5 million) trade, should begin to stabilise next week as large investors finished accumulating the large-cap stocks.
On Friday the bourse suspended industrial boilermaker Rafako trade indefinitely due to the southern Polish flooding after having done the same to ZEW the day before.

Analysts said some investors on Friday might have fled from shares of non-ferrous metals smelter Olawa, down eight percent in low turnover, for flood-water fears, though the stock did see stronger buying after price fixing.
